skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development

skills.name: troubleshooting

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. // Memory Region — Specifications
5. //
6. // A memory region is a contiguous, non-wrapping half-open byte interval of the
7. // address space, `[start, start + size)`, tagged with metadata
8. // (type / permissions / cache policy). `TruncatedMemoryRegion<T>` is the same
9. // interval additionally constrained so both endpoints are page-aligned, making
10. // it directly usable for frame/page booking. Both region types share the single
11. // `MemoryRegionView` abstraction (the truncated wrapper forwards `view()` to its
12. // inner region).
13. //
14. // Addresses are abstracted to `int` through the universal `spec_addr` projection
15. // (defined in `page.spec.rs`, `pub uninterp spec fn spec_addr<T: Address>`),
16. // exactly as `PageAligned<T>` does. Using `spec_addr` — rather than a
17. // `T: View<V = int>` bound on the `View` impl — is what lets the `View` (and the
18. // `@`-based accessor contracts) be stated for a bare `T: Address`: the
19. // address-family `View` impls are all `cfg(verus_keep_ghost)`-gated and the
20. // generic exec `impl<T: Address> ...` blocks carry no `View` bound, so a
21. // conditional `View<V = int>` bound would make `self@` untypable inside the
22. // accessors. `spec_page_size()` is the canonical page size, re-exported from
23. // `crate::hal::mem`.
24. 
25. verus! {
26. 
27. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
28. use crate::hal::mem::spec_addr;
29. 
30. // Abstract value of a memory region: the geometry `(start, size)` (in bytes,
31. // as mathematical integers) plus the three metadata tags callers observe.
32. pub struct MemoryRegionView {
33.     /// First valid byte address of the region. Equals the `start` supplied at
34.     /// construction; for the truncated variant it is page-aligned. Also the
35.     /// `Ord` key for both region types.
36.     pub start: int,
37.     /// Length of the region in bytes. The interval is `[start, start + size)`.
38.     /// For the truncated variant it is a multiple of the page size.
39.     pub size: int,
40.     /// Classification of the region (Usable / Reserved / Mmio / Bad).
41.     pub typ: MemoryRegionType,
42.     /// Access permissions granted over the region.
43.     pub perm: AccessPermission,
44.     /// Optional MMIO caching policy; `None` for non-MMIO regions.
45.     pub cache_policy: Option<MmioCachePolicy>,
46. }
47. 
48. impl MemoryRegionView {
49.     /// Non-empty, non-wrapping interval lying within the address space. This is
50.     /// the geometry every constructed region guarantees and that caller
51.     /// arithmetic (`size - 1`, `start + size - 1`, `size / FRAME_SIZE`) relies
52.     /// on: `size >= 1` (`new` rejects `size == 0`) and the inclusive end
53.     /// `start + size - 1` never overflows the widest address representation.
54.     pub open spec fn wf_geometry(self) -> bool {
55.         &&& self.size >= 1
56.         &&& self.start >= 0
57.         &&& self.start + self.size <= usize::MAX as int + 1
58.     }
59. 
60.     /// Exclusive end of the half-open interval `[start, end)`.
61.     pub open spec fn spec_end(self) -> int {
62.         self.start + self.size
63.     }
64. 
65.     /// Inclusive last byte address (callers compute `start + size - 1`).
66.     pub open spec fn spec_last(self) -> int {
67.         self.start + self.size - 1
68.     }
69. 
70.     /// Whether `addr` lies in `[start, start + size)`.
71.     pub open spec fn contains(self, addr: int) -> bool {
72.         self.start <= addr < self.start + self.size
73.     }
74. 
75.     /// State transition of `MemoryRegion::set_cache_policy`: only the cache
76.     /// policy changes; geometry and the other tags are preserved (`..self`).
77.     pub open spec fn spec_set_cache_policy(self, policy: MmioCachePolicy) -> MemoryRegionView {
78.         MemoryRegionView { cache_policy: Some(policy), ..self }
79.     }
80. }
81. 
82. // `MemoryRegion<T>` abstracts to its geometry plus tags. The `view()` is
83. // `closed`: callers reference `self@.start` / `self@.size` but the field-to-
84. // storage mapping (and the `spec_addr` projection of the typed `start`) does not
85. // leak. Unconditional over `T: Address` (see module comment).
86. impl<T: Address> View for MemoryRegion<T> {
87.     type V = MemoryRegionView;
88. 
89.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> MemoryRegionView {
90.         MemoryRegionView {
91.             start: spec_addr(&self.start),
92.             size: self.size as int,
93.             typ: self.typ,
94.             perm: self.perm,
95.             cache_policy: self.cache_policy,
96.         }
97.     }
98. }
99. 
100. // `TruncatedMemoryRegion<T>` is the same interval with a stronger invariant; its
101. // `view()` forwards to the inner `MemoryRegion<PageAligned<T>>`.
102. impl<T: Address> View for TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
103.     type V = MemoryRegionView;
104. 
105.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> MemoryRegionView {
106.         self.0@
107.     }
108. }
109. 
110. // Well-formedness of a base memory region: non-empty, non-wrapping geometry.
111. impl<T: Address> MemoryRegion<T> {
112.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
113.         self@.wf_geometry()
114.     }
115. }
116. 
117. // Well-formedness of a truncated region: base geometry plus page alignment of
118. // both endpoints (established by `TruncatedMemoryRegion::new`'s `align_up`), so
119. // `size / FRAME_SIZE` is exact and `start` needs no re-alignment.
120. impl<T: Address> TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
121.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
122.         &&& self@.wf_geometry()
123.         &&& self@.start % spec_page_size() == 0
124.         &&& self@.size % spec_page_size() == 0
125.     }
126. }
127. 
128. } // verus!
129.

1. # TCB Allowed List — Nanvix phys-mm
2. 
3. Any `external_body` outside this list must be removed.
4. 
5. ## Allowed `external_body`
6. 
7. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/mod.rs::book_physical_memory_regions` — iterates a std
8.   `alloc::collections::LinkedList` via `for region in list.iter()`. The build
9.   toolchain's `vstd` (`/mnt/toolchain/verus/vstd`) ships ghost-iterator specs only
10.   for `slice`/`vec`/`VecDeque`/`BTree*`/`Hash*` iterators, **not** `LinkedList`, and
11.   the orphan rule forbids supplying `View`/`ForLoopGhostIterator` impls for the
12.   foreign `linked_list::Iter` from the `kernel` crate (E0117). Genuine Verus
13.   front-end limitation, not a proof gap or code bug — full analysis in
14.   `verus-unsupported.md`. The abstract booking effect is specified over
15.   `PhysMemView` and discharged (no `admit`) by
16.   `lemma_book_region_reserves_region_frames` in `mod.proof.rs`. `ensures` keeps the
17.   caller-relevant guarantee: allocator stays initialized and well-formed.
18. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/mod.rs::book_mmio_regions` — same std-`LinkedList`
19.   iteration limitation as above. Abstract effect (skip-if-not-covered; book tracked
20.   frames) discharged by `lemma_book_mmio_skip_untracked` /
21.   `lemma_book_mmio_books_tracked`. `ensures` keeps allocator initialized and
22.   well-formed across booking.
23. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref`
24. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref_mut`
25. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::clear`- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc` — materializes a
26.   `&'static mut [u8; N]` from a backend-provided address (`usize as *mut`); raw-memory
27.   op Verus cannot verify without a `PointsTo` for the externally-owned `BssStorage`
28.   region. Mirrors `src/libs/raw-array`. `ensures` states alignment + in-bounds over
29.   the abstract `bump_view`.
30. - `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc_as` — delegates to
31.   `alloc` and re-materializes the slot as `&'static mut MaybeUninit<T>`; same rationale.
32.   `ensures` adds the `size_of::<T>()`/`align_of::<T>()` vs `(N, A)` guard arms.
33. 
34. ## Skip / exclude from current proof target
35. 
36. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::get_mut`
37. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::init`
38. 
39. ## Allowed `external_body` — frame allocator core (`frame.rs`)
40. 
41. `frame.rs` is now the proof target. Two layers form the trust boundary of the
42. global frame-allocator singleton; everything else in the module (the `frame::*`
43. free-function shims) is **body-verified** against these contracts.
44. 
45. ### 1. The singleton bridge: `instance()`
46. 
47. `instance()` returns `&'static mut Inner` obtained from the module-level
48. `static mut INSTANCE` via `unsafe { INSTANCE.assume_init_mut() }`. The verifier
49. does not support `static mut` paths, and a zero-argument uninterpreted
50. `phys_view()` cannot be tied to that static by any verifiable means. `instance()`
51. is therefore the bridge axiom: `requires phys_view().initialized` (the real panic
52. gate) and `ensures (*result).inv() && (*result)@ == phys_view().frames`. This is
53. what lets the query shims (`is_covered`, `refcount`) be fully body-verified.
54. 
55. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::instance` — `static mut` singleton accessor;
56.   bridges the live `Inner` to the abstract `phys_view().frames`.
57. 
58. ### 2. The `Inner::*` methods
59. 
60. Each `Inner::*` method has a rich, do-not-modify `old(self)@ → final(self)@`
61. transition contract, but its **body** cannot be translated by Verus: every method
62. uses the `error!` / `debug_assert_eq!` macros (whose expansion needs
63. `core::fmt::Arguments`, unsupported — the same limitation already recorded for
64. `UserFrame::drop`) and the `arch` newtypes `FrameNumber` / `FrameAddress`
65. (external types with no `external_type_specification`). They are `external_body`
66. with their pre-existing `#[verus_spec]` contracts honored as trust boundaries.
67. 
68. - `Inner::alloc`, `Inner::alloc_contiguous`, `Inner::free`, `Inner::share`,
69.   `Inner::refcount`, `Inner::book`, `Inner::is_covered`, `Inner::alloc_range`
70.   (all in `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs`).
71. 
72. ### Note on the body-verified shims
73. 
74. The `frame::*` free-function shims are no longer `external_body`. The pure-query
75. shims `is_covered` and `refcount` are proven outright via the `instance()` bridge.
76. The aggregate query shim `free_count` is also fully body-verified via
77. `lemma_free_count` (`frame.proof.rs`): it counts the clear bitmap indices as the
78. image of an injective `i -> i * page_size` map and discharges
79. `free_frames.len() + usage == num_bits` without any `admit()`.
80. 
81. The mutating reservation shims (`alloc`, `alloc_contiguous`, `book`,
82. `alloc_range`, `share`) are body-verified and carry the **strong** post-state
83. contract via the `tracked PhysAuth` carrier threaded through `&mut`: each names
84. both `old(auth)@` (pre-state) and `final(auth)@` (post-state) and asserts the

 function is therefore `external_body` with its `#[verus_spec]` contract honored as a
 trust boundary — the same pattern as `FrameAddress::into_raw_value`. The contract is
 the real caller guarantee (newtype identity + page-alignment invariant), not a
 weakening; it is discharged when the `Address` trait and the `Alignment` encoding are
 verified.
 
 - `src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/address/aligned/page.rs::PageAligned::from_address` —
   validating, identity-preserving constructor. On success `result@ == spec_addr(&addr)`
   and `result.inv()`; on failure `spec_addr(&addr) % spec_page_size() != 0`; success
   holds iff the input address is page-aligned. Removed when `sys::mm::Address` /
   `Alignment` are verified.
 
 ## Allowed `assume_specification` — `hal::mem::PageAligned` `Address::into_raw_value`
 
 `<PageAligned<T> as Address>::into_raw_value` is a method of the external
 **`sys::mm::Address`** trait. A per-method `external_body`/`#[verus_spec]` would
 require marking the whole `impl Address for PageAligned<T>` verified, which currently
 triggers a Verus front-end panic (`vir/src/traits.rs:511 assertion failed:
 !method_impls.contains(&p)`) on this generic trait impl. It is therefore specced with
 `assume_specification` in `page.spec.rs`, mirroring the existing
 `<PageAligned<T> as Address>::from_raw_value` trust boundary (`kframe.spec.rs`) and the
 `::arch::mem::PAGE_SIZE` boundary (`frame.rs`). The `@`-based contract is expressible
 because `PageAligned<T>: View` now holds for every `T: Address` (unconditional `View`
 delegating to the ghost `spec_addr`). The real obligation is the inner
 `<T as Address>::into_raw_value` newtype identity, discharged when the `Address` trait
 is verified.
 
 - `<crate::hal::mem::PageAligned<T> as crate::hal::mem::Address>::into_raw_value`
   (declared in `src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/address/aligned/page.spec.rs`).
   `ensures result as int == addr@`.
 
 ## Allowed `external_type_specification` — `hal::mem::types::address::phys` (proof target)
 
 `PhysicalAddress` is the proof target of the `hal::mem::types::address::phys`
 module. It projects to / from the `arch` crate's `FrameNumber`, a foreign type
 from a non-Verus-enabled crate with no `View`/datatype registration reachable
 here (orphan rule). To let `FrameNumber` appear in spec-fn parameters and the
 library-edge `assume_specification`s, it is registered as an opaque external
 datatype via `external_type_specification` + `external_body` — the exact idiom
 already approved for `ExLinkedList` (`mm/phys/mod.spec.rs`). Its internals are not
 modeled; its abstract index is projected by the uninterpreted
 `spec_frame_raw_value`.
 
 - `src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/address/phys.spec.rs::ExFrameNumber` —
   `external_type_specification` wrapper registering the foreign `arch::FrameNumber`
   as opaque. No body verified; carries no abstract guarantee beyond opacity.
 
 ## Allowed `assume_specification` — `hal::mem::types::address::phys` library edge
 
 `PhysicalAddress`'s verified constructors/projections call `arch`/`sys`
 library-edge items whose home crates are not yet Verus-enabled. Each is specced
 with `assume_specification` in `phys.spec.rs`, mirroring the existing
 `::arch::mem::PAGE_SIZE` (`frame.rs`) and `sys::mm::Address`
 (`kframe.spec.rs` / `page.spec.rs`) boundaries the codebase already draws. The
 contracts state only the load-bearing newtype-identity / positivity / range facts
 the proofs rely on; they introduce no new observable guarantee and are removed
 when `arch`/`sys` are verified.
 
 - `::arch::mem::FRAME_SIZE` — `result == spec_page_size() && spec_page_size() > 0`.
 - `::arch::mem::FRAME_SHIFT` — `result < usize::BITS && pow2(result) == spec_page_size()`.
 - `VirtualAddress::new` — `result@ == value as int` (newtype constructor).
 - `<VirtualAddress as Address>::into_raw_value` — `result as int == addr@`.
 - `FrameNumber::into_raw_value` — projects index in `0 ..= spec_max_frame_number()`.
 - `FrameNumber::from_raw_value` — `Some` iff `value <= spec_max_frame_number()`,
   preserving the index; `None` otherwise.
   (all declared in `src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/address/phys.spec.rs`.)
